thread.title: Capitol Report: FBI reportedly probing whether Russian money went to NRA to help Trump | Most Americans support DACA, poll finds

title: Capitol Report: FBI reportedly probing whether Russian money went to NRA to help Trump | Most Americans support DACA, poll finds
text:
10:17 a.m. ET Share 
House to vote on bill to avoid shutdown 
By Fiscal policy reporter Getty Images The FBI is reportedly probing whether a top Russian banker illegally funneled money to the NRA to help Donald Trump win the White House. 
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is probing whether a top Russian banker with Kremlin ties illegally funneled money to the National Rifle Association to help Donald Trump win the presidency, McClatchy reported. 
McClatchy’s report said FBI investigators have focused on the activities of Alexander Torshin , the deputy governor of Russia’s central bank, who is known for his close relationships with both Russian President Vladimir Putin and the NRA. It is illegal to use foreign money to influence federal elections. The news comes as Special Counsel Robert Mueller’s investigation of Russian meddling in the 2016 election has been heating up. McClatchy’s report cited two sources familiar with the matter, and said an FBI spokesman declined to comment. The NRA didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment, McClatchy said. 
Support for DACA: Nearly nine in 10 Americans favor allowing young immigrants who came to the U.S. illegally as children to remain in the country, a CBS News poll finds . But Americans are divided over whether supporting the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program is worth risking a shutdown of the federal government. Democrats think it is; Republicans do not, according to the poll. See more: CBS News poll: Most Americans support DACA, but oppose border wall https://t.co/noBoMM6W6C pic.twitter.com/FQqdUBcF15 — CBS News (@CBSNews) January 18, 2018 
Tech lobby defends visa program: Axios reports the Information Technology Industry Council, a major tech lobby, sent a letter to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services calling for the H-4 visa rule to be upheld . USCIS is expected to end the H-4 work eligibility program, which allows the spouses of H-1B holders with pending green cards to work legally in the U.S. The council lobbies for companies including Amazon AMZN, -0.13% , Apple AAPL, +0.09% and Facebook FB, +1.24% . 
House to vote on bill averting shutdown: The House plans to vote Thursday on a bill that would fund the federal government through Feb. 16, averting a shutdown. “There’s still some work to do, but I think it will pass,” Rep. Tom Cole, an Oklahoma Republican and a top appropriator, told the Hill. The bill doesn’t include a DACA fix. But it could be hard for Democrats to block the bill since it includes a six-year extension of funding for the Children’s Health Insurance Program . It also delays Obamacare taxes. The federal government is funded through Friday. More from MarketWatch
